title: BLACK-BOX RELIABILITY CERTIFICATION FOR AI AGENTS VIA SELF-CONSISTENCY SAMPLING AND CONFORMAL CALIBRATION

bias_targets.methodology: Formal mathematical decomposition of Mean Squared Error (MSE) into variance and irreducible judge bias (such as position bias, verbosity preference, and self-preference). This is empirically validated by comparing the accuracy and coverage gaps of LLM-as-judge evaluations against conformal prediction models across standard benchmarks.

Using conformal prediction set sizes as a diagnostic tool. The framework mathematically proves and empirically demonstrates that an AI agent's systematic errors (statistical bias) force the prediction set size to increase, thereby making the bias transparently visible rather than hiding it in point-estimate scores.
